header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood CSM); Priya Desai, Liam O'Connor, Nora Patel, Ethan Ross (Enterprise Retail)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review model selection and pinning strategy. Discussed tradeoffs between higher-quality base models vs quantized variants for cost, pinning approach, rollback/fallback policies, and next steps for benchmarks and security onboarding.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC sync for Enterprise Retail, we wanted to go over model selection and pinning approach, and any blockers.
[00:22] Priya: hey thanks, yes hi all, we've run some initial evals last week, saw some interesting tradeoffs on cost vs latency.
[00:35] Diego: quick FYI I re-ran the smaller set overnight, so I have numbers for redwood-llama-70b-v2 and a quantized 8-bit alpaca variant.
[00:50] Liam: I flagged infra concerns, our SLO is p95 < 220ms for storefront suggestions under load, is that still the main target?
[01:05] Priya: yes that's correct, and recall/accuracy target is around >92% on our retrieval prompts.
[01:20] Maya: clear, we should talk about pinning the model to ensure reproducibility; two strategies: pin to the full 70B v2 float or pin to a quantized variant to save cost but risk slight regressions.
[01:42] Nora: can you explain the rollback story? if we pin and see regressions, how fast can we roll back?
[01:55] Diego: rollback is pretty quick — with Redwood Dedicated we can route traffic to a fallback model version or fallback instance pool, it's a config change + 1-2 minute rollout typically, but depends on KV cache warmup.
[02:18] Ethan: when you say KV cache warmup, we're worried about latency spikes during those transitions, right?
[02:30] Diego: yeah, if the warmed KV cache is specific to a model on the host, switching to another variant can incur cold-start token costs, p95 jumps for first N requests. We can mitigate with staged traffic ramp and keep a small warm pool.
[02:52] Priya: what's the naming of the variants you ran? so we record exact pinned model strings.
[03:00] Diego: I called them rwlab-redwood-llama-70b-v2 and rwlab-alpaca-34b-8bit-q4, although the transcription may show alpaca-34b-8, but full tag will be in the bench sheet.
[03:18] Maya: important to capture the exact artifact hash/version, we'll attach to the pilot run.
[03:30] Priya: ok on accuracy: the 70b v2 float did best, recall 94.1%, p95 latency 260ms on our test rig; the alpaca-34b quantized got recall 90.3% but p95 170ms.
[03:50] Nora: so the float meets recall but misses latency SLO; quantized meets latency but misses recall.
[04:05] Diego: exactly, tradeoff is clear. Another option is a routing policy: latency-sensitive endpoints route to the quantized model, and back-office or high-accuracy paths route to 70b v2. Redwood's smart routing supports per-route pinning.
[04:28] Maya: that's a strong pattern, and we can use automatic fallback if the primary capacity is saturated. Also consider prefix caching for common prompts to reduce cost and latency.
[04:45] Priya: curious about cost delta, can you ballpark difference for our 100 qps steady state?
[04:56] Diego: rough estimates: float 70b v2 on Dedicated - about 3.8x the per-token cost of the quantized 34b. So over time quantized saves materially; I'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Ethan: security question — if we pin to a model image, do we get reproducible audit logs and KMS key access per-run?
[05:22] Maya: yes, with Private/Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS and per-request audit logs are available, we'll share the onboarding checklist.
[05:35] Liam: any compliance gotchas with quantized models vs original weights?
[05:42] Diego: not typically, the artifact is still the model binary; we provide the build provenance and checksum. If your compliance team wants binary-level attestation, we can coordinate that.
[05:56] Priya: thinking about pinning strategy — is it better to pin to a major version and allow minor updates, or pin to exact hash?
[06:06] Maya: recommendation: pin to exact artifact for pilot validation, then for prod you can pin to a semantic version that we control and gate via canary. Exact pin gives you deterministic results for A/B and evals.
[06:22] Nora: what about rollbacks for regressions detected by evaluation harness? how are regressions detected and automated?
[06:33] Diego: Redwood Optimize can run evals on a prompt set and trigger alerts; rollbacks aren't usually automatic without human approval but you can configure automatic fallback routing if latency/cost or quality thresholds are breached.
[06:50] Priya: can we do canary on a percentage split and auto-fallback on quality regressions?
[06:58] Diego: yes, you can set a canary and set a quality threshold tied to eval metrics; if the canary falls below threshold we can fail it and revert traffic.
[07:10] Maya: action item: Diego will run a 1k query bench to get p50/p95 and throughput numbers and include model artifact names.
[07:20] Priya: thanks. Also we want to test mixed routing — suggestions frontend needs low latency so will prefer quantized, while cart support backend can use float.
[07:34] Diego: we can demo per-route config next week; for now I'll focus on bench numbers.
[07:45] Nora: any notes on sequence length — our prompts average 240 tokens, but with retrieval embeddings could go to 600 sometimes. How does that affect these numbers?
[07:58] Diego: sequence length scales cost and latency; the 70b float suffers more. For longer contexts, quantized variants sometimes have less overhead per-token due to optimized kernels but accuracy may degrade. We'll include sequence-length stratified results.
[08:18] Ethan: on KMS — we need an HSM-backed key for model encryption and strict access controls, can Redwood support that?
[08:27] Maya: yes, we support BYOK with HSM-backed KMS; we'll share the architectural doc and checklist.
[08:40] Liam: about fallback pools — if a Dedicated pool is saturated, what's the fallback latency to Hosted?
[08:49] Diego: Hosted fallback can add cross-region latency and also different throttles; expect an additional 80-150ms depending on region and model. It's a safety net but not ideal for latency-sensitive routes.
[09:05] Priya: could we instead keep a small hot pool of cheaper instances to handle bursts?
[09:12] Diego: yes that's a common pattern: small hot warm pool plus autoscale for longer bursts. There is a cost tradeoff.
[09:25] Maya: let's capture pricing and cost tradeoffs as a separate doc. I'll attach the sample pricing model for Dedicated pilot.
[09:35] Priya: another ask — we need deterministic outputs for A/B testing, how do we ensure model determinism across variants?
[09:46] Diego: determinism comes from fixed seeds and pinned artifact. Quantization can introduce some nondeterminism at the token-generation microlevel, but it's usually minor. For strict comparatives you should pin exact artifacts and generation params.
[10:02] Nora: what about model size for embedding rival features — are we standardizing on one embeddings model?
[10:10] Maya: embeddings are out-of-scope for today's sync, but we can note it: typically we choose an embeddings model pinned separately.
[10:18] Priya: ok, for this pilot we care about the suggestion generator only.
[10:24] Diego: I'll add bench results broken down by sequence length, load profile, and cold vs warmed KV cache.
[10:35] Priya: thanks. On rollback: can we keep a short-lived snapshot of KV caches to warm new instances faster?
[10:45] Diego: we can snapshot prefix caches for common prefixes, but KV cache for autoregressive decoding is token-level state; snapshotting and loading is doable but adds complexity. We usually rely on warm pools.
[10:58] Ethan: security note — we need to see proof that rollback artifacts are immutable and auditable.
[11:05] Maya: we'll include artifact checksums and the audit log schema in the security packet.
[11:12] Priya: timeline: we want a decision by next Friday to start pilot the week of 11/23. Is that feasible?
[11:22] Maya: yes if bench numbers and security checklist are clear. Diego and I will move quickly on the bench and pricing.
[11:32] Nora: any open blockers from our side?
[11:37] Priya: Ethan needs to confirm KMS vendor and compliance checklist but otherwise we're good.
[11:45] Diego: question — do you want us to include a fallback to a smaller float model (eg 30-40B float) instead of the 34B quantized? Might be middle ground.
[11:57] Priya: maybe, include as an option in the bench table.
[12:04] Maya: recap of next steps and action items, Diego to bench, Maya to send pricing + security docs, Priya/Ethan to finalize success criteria and KMS contacts. We'll meet same time next week.
[12:20] Priya: thanks everyone.
[12:24] Maya: thanks, meeting adjourned.
